summary: Split app/services/sessions.py (518 lines at HEAD) into a package with a barrel: rows.py (row JSON helpers plan_node_dict/question_dict), session.py (constants PHASES/GROUNDING_MODES + SessionService CRUD, retrieval helpers, message persistence), turn.py (SUFFICIENCY_NOTICE + TurnMixin SSE turn/retry generators + _error_event), and __init__.py barrel re-exporting the full public surface so every existing `from app.services.sessions import X` keeps working unchanged
final_report: Split app/services/sessions.py (518 lines) into app/services/sessions/ package with barrel. __init__.py re-exports SessionService, plan_node_dict, question_dict, PHASES, GROUNDING_MODES, SUFFICIENCY_NOTICE. rows.py (25) holds plan_node_dict/question_dict verbatim. session.py (278) holds PHASES + GROUNDING_MODES + SessionService(TurnMixin) with CRUD/retrieval/persistence methods moved verbatim. turn.py (231) holds SUFFICIENCY_NOTICE + TurnMixin (turn, _emit_sufficiency_notice, retry_last_turn, _last_user_message) + _error_event, verbatim. Import smoke ok. compileall clean. Full pytest: 211 passed. Zero import churn: all existing importers (api/chat, api/sessions, services/learning, services/plans, services/teach, tests) go through the barrel.
notes: Split rationale: option (b) TurnMixin — session.py would be ~480 lines if turn methods stayed, too close to the 500-line soft limit, and turn.py keeps SSE concerns isolated. Import-cycle resolution: SUFFICIENCY_NOTICE was used only by _emit_sufficiency_notice, so it moved to turn.py; turn.py imports nothing from session.py at runtime (Session/LLMClient annotations only under TYPE_CHECKING, lazy via future annotations), so session.py -> turn.py is a one-way edge with no cycle. GROUNDING_MODES/PHASES stay in session.py where they gate CRUD. Dropped the original's unused GroundingMode import (only used in app/llm/messages.py). Barrel uses relative imports with # noqa: F401 matching app/services/extraction/__init__.py style. git detects the split as a rename sessions.py -> sessions/session.py (52%), preserving history.
